name: Tesamorelin
lead: Tesamorelin (brand names Egrifta, Egrifta SV and Egrifta WR) is a synthetic analogue of growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) made by Theratechnologies of Canada. It was approved by the US FDA in November 2010 for reducing excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy and is given by daily subcutaneous injection. [1][9][3]

The appearance link is the midsection. In the approved population, trials measured loss of visceral (deep abdominal) fat, and the pooled phase 3 analysis also reported improved patient and physician ratings of belly profile and less belly-related distress. [5] Tesamorelin stimulates the pituitary to release endogenous growth hormone in a pulsatile pattern, raising IGF-1 and promoting lipolysis, with a particular effect on visceral fat. [3][1]

The label states it is not indicated for weight loss management, as its effect on weight is neutral, and that long-term cardiovascular safety has not been established. [3] In bodybuilding and peptide forums it is discussed as a growth-hormone secretagogue, often paired with ipamorelin, for fat loss and raising IGF-1. [24][21][22]

Approval and trial evidence cover HIV-associated abdominal fat. Trials have not tested the drug for fat loss in people without HIV lipodystrophy or for facial appearance, and it is not known to remove fat from any specific site selectively. In 2026 the FDA issued warning letters to online sellers marketing tesamorelin as a research product. [26]

angle.text: Tesamorelin is a prescription GHRH analogue whose approved effect is a reduction in visceral abdominal fat in adults with HIV lipodystrophy, which trial participants and clinicians rated as improving the look of the belly. Forum users discuss off-label use for fat loss and body composition, which the trials did not study.

infobox: Excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy [3]
44 amino acids of human GHRH plus a trans-3-hexenoyl group; molar mass about 5136 g/mol [1]
Prescription-only; FDA treats unapproved sales as unapproved new drugs [3][26]

paras: Egrifta SV is indicated for the reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy. The label's limitations state that it is not indicated for weight loss, that no data show improved adherence to antiretroviral therapy, and that treatment should be reconsidered in patients who do not reduce visceral fat. [3]

HIV-associated lipodystrophy refers to changes in fat distribution in people on antiretroviral therapy, including central fat gain. A 2011 review describes the condition as distressing, associated with cardiovascular risk, and as having few effective treatments before tesamorelin, since switching antiretrovirals, insulin sensitisers, surgery and fillers gave limited or temporary benefit. [29]

Forum users describe using tesamorelin off-label in combination with other peptides such as ipamorelin, or alongside testosterone and anabolic compounds, to raise IGF-1 and reduce fat. [24][19][25] One poster on T Nation argues that GH-related products lower fat and cites tesamorelin's approval as support. [23] These uses are outside the approved indication, and the label's evidence concerns HIV lipodystrophy. [3]

Native GHRH is broken down quickly in the body by dipeptidyl peptidase, so tesamorelin was engineered with a modified amino terminus to be more stable and longer lasting; it was previously known by the code TH9507. [1][29] The earlier option of recombinant growth hormone reduced visceral fat in HIV lipodystrophy but caused side effects such as oedema, joint pain and higher blood glucose, which motivated a GH-releasing approach. [29]

Two phase 3 trials of about 400 people each ran for 26 weeks, with the first published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2007 and a pooled analysis in 2010. [4][5] The FDA approved Egrifta in November 2010. [9] A newer F8 formulation, Egrifta WR, was approved in March 2025; it is reconstituted weekly rather than daily, uses a smaller injection volume and is described as bioequivalent to the earlier product. A January 2024 Complete Response Letter from the FDA had preceded that approval. [28]

In 2025 Theratechnologies also reported a supply disruption for Egrifta SV after a contract manufacturer's voluntary shutdown in 2024; regular distribution resumed after an FDA supplement approval in April 2025. [28]

The pivotal trial randomised 412 people with HIV, most of them men, who had abdominal fat accumulation, to daily tesamorelin or placebo for 26 weeks. Visceral fat measured by CT fell about 15 percent with tesamorelin and rose about 5 percent with placebo; triglycerides and cholesterol ratio improved and IGF-1 rose, and more people on tesamorelin withdrew because of adverse events. [4]

A pooled analysis of two phase 3 trials with 806 participants reported a visceral fat treatment effect of about minus 15 percent at week 26, no significant change in subcutaneous abdominal fat, and improved belly-related distress and patient and physician ratings of belly profile. Reductions were maintained at week 52 in people who continued treatment. [5] A 2011 review notes that visceral fat returned after stopping treatment. [29]

A 2014 JAMA trial at Massachusetts General Hospital randomised 50 adults to tesamorelin or placebo for six months and reported a visceral fat treatment effect of minus 42 cm2 and a reduction in liver fat. [7] A 2024 trial examined people with HIV on integrase inhibitors. [10]

A Lancet HIV trial in 61 adults with HIV and fatty liver disease compared tesamorelin with placebo for 12 months and reported an absolute difference in hepatic fat fraction of minus 4.1 percent; 35 percent of the tesamorelin group fell below the 5 percent threshold versus 4 percent of the placebo group. Glucose measures did not differ between groups. [8] A related analysis examined liver transcriptomic signatures. [15]

Tesamorelin has also been tested in type 2 diabetes, in obese people with reduced growth hormone, and for cognition and inflammatory markers. [11][12][13][14][16] Pharmacy-journal reviews summarise efficacy and safety in HIV lipodystrophy. [9]

The most commonly reported adverse reactions include joint pain, injection-site reactions, fluid retention and peripheral oedema, diarrhoea and glucose intolerance. [3][1] The label warns of increased risk of neoplasms, elevated IGF-1, fluid retention, glucose intolerance or diabetes, hypersensitivity and injection-site reactions; pre-existing malignancy should be inactive before starting and IGF-1 should be monitored. [3] A review of an FDA briefing reported higher odds of diabetes with tesamorelin in trials, and more patients with IGF-1 above the normal range; the long-term effects of chronic GH-axis stimulation are described as unclear. [29]

The drug is contraindicated in pregnancy, and in rats exposure during organogenesis caused hydrocephaly in offspring. [3] Wikipedia also lists contraindication in hypothalamic-pituitary axis disruption such as pituitary tumour, head irradiation or hypopituitarism. [1]

Tesamorelin binds human GHRH receptors with potency similar to the endogenous hormone and stimulates synthesis and pulsatile release of growth hormone, which is anabolic and lipolytic. [3] The modified N-terminus makes it more stable and more resistant to cleavage by dipeptidyl peptidase than native GHRH. [1] Its main mechanisms for reducing fat mass are lipolysis and lower triglycerides. [1]
Wikipedia gives its bioavailability as at most about 4 percent, with an elimination half-life of roughly 26 to 38 minutes, cleared by proteolysis and the kidneys. [1]

Tesamorelin is a prescription medicine, and Wikipedia lists it as a prohibited substance under the World Anti-Doping Agency's rules. [1] In a letter dated 24 August 2026, the FDA told an online seller that it considers tesamorelin an unapproved new drug when marketed outside the approved application, and that 'research use only' labels did not change that view given the site's marketing and its sale of injection-related products. [26]
Reviews of peptide therapy in sports medicine and aesthetics describe a gray market of unapproved peptides outside regulatory oversight, with scarce rigorous human safety data. [17][18]

subs.h: Use in looksmaxxing and peptide communities
paras: T Nation threads discuss tesamorelin among growth-hormone peptides, with members comparing IGF-1 results from combinations with ipamorelin or CJC-1295 and noting that these secretagogues do not stimulate hunger the way some GHRPs do. [20][21][24][19] Posters also report using it alongside oxandrolone or testosterone and note its cost. [25][19] A looksmax.org thread asks how tesamorelin interacts with other GH peptide products. [30]

A September 2026 Forbes Australia report says gray-market sellers market tesamorelin for muscle growth and fat loss under a research-purposes label, that users sometimes use the shorthand 'tesa' to avoid content filters, and that podcaster Andrew Huberman has mentioned it in the context of sleep. The article describes people who reported severe reactions after peptide injections and notes that without product testing it is not possible to tell whether reactions came from the peptide or contaminants. [27]

Sports-medicine physician Thomas Kremen of UCLA Health, quoted by Forbes Australia, reviewed six popular peptides and described possible safety concerns and little evidence of benefit. [27] The Alliance for Pharmacy Compounding and consumer-safety groups have commented on peptide regulation, and the FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee has been reconsidering several peptides for the 503A bulk list, with tesamorelin not part of that vote. [27][31]
Safe Medicines notes an FDA warning letter in April 2026 to a Chinese producer of unfinished bulk peptides, including tesamorelin acetate, over sterility violations. [31]

Tesamorelin has randomised phase 3 data in HIV-associated abdominal fat [4][5][6][7], randomised data on liver fat in HIV-associated fatty liver disease [8][15], and smaller trials in type 2 diabetes, obesity with reduced growth hormone, cognition and inflammatory markers. [11][12][13][14] No published trial has tested tesamorelin for cosmetic fat loss in healthy people or for facial appearance.

lore.intro: Tesamorelin appears in T Nation and looksmax.org discussions of growth-hormone peptides, usually alongside ipamorelin or CJC-1295, with attention to IGF-1 numbers and fat loss. [20][21][24][30]

claims.claim: Tesamorelin plus ipamorelin raises IGF-1 more than other secretagogue blends.
claims.believers: Posters report IGF-1 rising to 300 or more with the pair, compared with lower values on CJC-1295 with DAC or on injected GH. [19][21][24]
claims.experts: Trials measured IGF-1 changes in people with HIV lipodystrophy, and the label notes tesamorelin raises IGF-1 and that prolonged elevation effects are unknown. [3][4]

claims.claim: Tesamorelin lowers fat, so GH-related products lower fat in general.
claims.believers: A poster points to its FDA approval for visceral fat as support for GH-axis drugs reducing fat. [23]
claims.experts: Approval and trials concern visceral fat in HIV lipodystrophy, where visceral fat fell about 15 percent; the label says it is not for weight loss. [3][4][5]

claims.claim: The tesamorelin/ipamorelin blend avoids growth hormone's side effects.
claims.believers: A poster with a family history of diabetes chose the blend because it supposedly lacks side effects of GH. [24]
claims.experts: The label warns of fluid retention, glucose intolerance, elevated IGF-1 and neoplasm risk, and an FDA briefing reported higher diabetes odds in trials. [3][29]

claims.claim: It does not stimulate hunger like some growth-hormone peptides.
claims.believers: A poster says only ghrelin-acting peptides cause hunger and that ipamorelin and tesamorelin do not. [20]
claims.experts: The label's adverse-reaction list does not feature appetite increase. [3]

claims.claim: Low-dose tesamorelin works for fat loss when stacked with anabolics.
claims.believers: Posters describe using it with oxandrolone or testosterone for results. [22][25]
claims.experts: No published trial has tested such combinations in healthy people. [7][11]

claims.claim: GH-axis drugs can change facial features at normal doses.
claims.believers: A T Nation thread asks whether growth hormone causes facial changes at low or normal doses and discusses tesamorelin blends. [19]
claims.experts: No published trial has examined facial changes with tesamorelin; its trials measured visceral fat and liver fat. [4][7]

claims.claim: Research-grade tesamorelin is equivalent to the prescription product.
claims.believers: Sellers label gray-market products as research peptides, and forum threads discuss tesamorelin blends obtained outside pharmacy channels. [27][30]
claims.experts: The FDA considers tesamorelin sold outside its approved application an unapproved new drug, and Forbes reports that gray-market products may not contain what the label states. [26][27]

claims.believers: Posters discuss tesamorelin among peptides used for fat loss and raising IGF-1 over extended periods. [24][22]
claims.experts: A 2011 review reports that visceral fat returned after treatment stopped, while continued use maintained the reduction. [29][5]
